Predictors of RSV positivity included younger admission age, male sex, non-Aboriginal ethnicity, a diagnosis of bronchiolitis and longer hospital stay. Our model showed good predictive accuracy (AUROC: 0.87). The respective sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive values were 58.4%, 92.2%, 68.6% and 88.3%. The predicted incidence rates of hospitalised RSV for children aged < 3 months was 43.7/1000 child-years (95% CI 42.1–45.4) compared with 31.7/1000 child-years (95% CI 30.3–33.1) from laboratory-confirmed RSV admissions. Findings from our study suggest that the true burden of RSV may be 30–57% higher than current estimates. Subject terms: Epidemiology, Viral infection
11: 
12: ## Introduction
13: 
14: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in young children worldwide, causing 3.2 million detected hospitalisation episodes every year 1 . The true burden is likely to be much greater, with approximately half of RSV-associated deaths estimated to occur outside of hospital 1 . In Australia, for every 100,000 hospitalised children aged < 5 years, an estimated 418 have RSV 2 . A recent population-based study in Western Australia (WA) conducted by our group reported pathogen-specific incidence rates of 247/100,000 child-years for RSV in children aged < 17 years 3 , with the highest burden among infants in their first 3 months of life (28.1/1000 child-years) 4 . RSV is most frequently associated with hospitalisations for acute bronchiolitis, but was also identified across other clinical diagnoses including pneumonia, unspecified acute lower respiratory infections, asthma, upper respiratory infections as well as non-specific viral diagnosis codes 3 , 5 .
15: 
16: Population-wide in our jurisdiction and elsewhere, there is no systematic approach to RSV testing, nor is it currently a notifiable disease, making estimates of RSV disease burden using microbiological testing datasets alone difficult. From our population-based study, only 10% of children aged < 17 years were ever tested for RSV and variable testing trends were seen between age groups and from year to year. Additionally, 54% of children hospitalised with respiratory infections did not have a corresponding microbiological test 3 . Improved estimates of RSV burden are required to inform future policy for RSV therapeutics and preventative strategies, as late-stage clinical trials of antivirals, maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies progress 3 , 6 .
17: 
18: Understanding the demographic and clinical predictors of RSV test positivity in different populations can aid in quantifying the under-ascertainment burden of RSV from standalone datasets. Ideally, a combination of clinical and laboratory data is needed. Such a study has been conducted in England for infants aged < 1 year, using hospitalisation data and RSV positive testing records 7 .
19: 
20: The aim of our study was to develop a prediction model to estimate the true incidence of RSV associated hospitalisations in children < 5 years of age in WA and to use these findings to determine the under-ascertainment fraction of RSV incidence using laboratory records alone.
21: 
22: ## Methods
23: 
24: ### Setting and data sources
25: 
26: WA covers the western third of Australia with a population of approximately 2.6 million people at 31 December 2019 8 . Three quarters of the population reside in the temperate climatic region of metropolitan Perth and its surrounds 9 . We conducted a population-based cohort study using administrative linked data of all births in WA (1996 to 2012), as previously reported 3 , 10 . Data sources used for this study included the Midwives Notifications System, which includes perinatal information on > 99% of births in WA 11 , Birth and Death Registries, Hospital Morbidity Data Collection and PathWest Laboratory Medicine Database (PathWest). Data were probabilistically linked using best practice protocols through the WA Data Linkage Branch 12 .
27: 
28: #### Hospital data
29: 
30: Hospitalisation records, herein referred to as hospital admissions, with an admission and discharge date between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2012 were included, to match the same time period when routine laboratory data were available. We included all admissions in children aged < 5 years in WA with any diagnosis using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems,10th Revision, Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM) codes. As per previous analyses of these data, interhospital transfers were collapsed 3 , 10 .
31: 
32: #### Laboratory data
33: 
34: We extracted PathWest testing records of RSV from respiratory specimens with a specimen collection date between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2012. We then linked these records with hospitalisation records from individuals from the birth cohort when respiratory specimens were collected 48 h before or after the admission date, as per our previous analyses 3 , 10 . The laboratory records were linked to the admission closest to the date of specimen collection when the same child had multiple admissions for different reasons within 48 h. During the early study period, RSV was predominantly detected through immunofluorescence antigen detection (65%) and viral culture on respiratory specimens and complement-fixation tests (CFT) on serum while, gradually, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) on respiratory specimens was more frequently used 4 , 10 . Using assembled data from hospital and PathWest records, we then identified our source population defined as children in the cohort who had a hospitalisation for any reason in the first 5 years of life with RSV testing records during the study period (n = 37,784 hospitalisations). After exclusion of 3,801 records with missing data for one or more of the variables, we finally included 33,983 hospitalisations with RSV testing records in the final prediction model. Similarly, after excluding observations with missing data, we estimated RSV burden in 321,825 records of hospitalised children under 5 years of age during the study period (Fig. 1 ).
35: 
36: **Figure 1.** Flow diagram of datasets.
37: 
38: ### Statistical analysis
39: 
40: #### Developing prediction models
41: 
42: A multivariable logistic regression model was fitted to identify predictors of RSV-positivity (binary outcome) amongst children younger than 5 years who were hospitalised and tested for RSV in WA during the study period (2000–2012). We used a robust standard error estimation adjusting for correlated observations due to children having multiple admissions over the study period 13 . A total of 27 candidate predictors for the prediction models were selected based on a comprehensive literature review, including previous work in our setting 14 and clinical plausibility.
43: 
44: Directed acyclic graphs (DAG) were used to inform the choice of these predictors. In modern epidemiology, DAGs are used as a tool in causal inference to identify and demonstrate knowledge, theories and assumptions about causal relationships between variables 15 , 16 . Causal inference principles have recently been more widely applied in prediction models 17 , 18 . The minimal set of variables identified by DAGs included child age, sex, delivery route (vaginal vs caesarean), season of admission, Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status, respectfully referred to as (Aboriginal/non-Aboriginal), as identified through a validated algorithm provided by the WA linkage branch 19 , maternal age (categorised), smoking during pregnancy (yes/no), socioeconomic status (in quantiles), numbers of siblings, gestational age (< 32 weeks, 32–36 weeks and 37 or more weeks), admission year, birth year, length of hospital stay (continuous), admission to intensive care unit (ICU) [binary], mechanical ventilation use during hospital admission (see below), maternal history of asthma (binary), any diagnosis code for acute bronchiolitis, pneumonia, bronchitis, unspecified acute lower respiratory infections (ALRI), asthma, URTI, whooping cough, influenza and diagnosis code for other infections including unspecified viral illness, convulsions, fever and cough, breathing abnormalities (refer to eTable 1 ). These specific codes were chosen based on our previous work that identified a positive detection of a respiratory virus in hospital admissions with these codes 10 . Further, we included season of birth and geographical region of residence to account for seasonality and climatic conditions (as a proxy) respectively (eTable 1 ). Our final prediction model also included a sine and cosine function as per the recommendation by Stolwijk and Edwards to account for the seasonal variation of RSV 20 , 21 .
45: 
46: Socioeconomic status (SES) was measured using Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA). Specifically, we used the Index of Relative Advantage and Disadvantage score, calculated at the collection district (CD) level by Australian Bureau of Statistics 22 .
47: 
48: A child was coded as admitted to an ICU if they spent at least one day in ICU as recorded on the Hospital Morbidity Data Collection. Mechanical ventilation was defined as receipt of at least an hour of continuous ventilatory support or having procedure codes (classified using the 7th edition of the Australian Classification of Health Interventions) for airway management, invasive or non-invasive ventilatory support (eTable 1 ).
49: 
50: #### Model specification and estimation
51: 
52: As part of model development, a stepwise backward selection approach using Akaike Information criterion (AIC) was performed. Stepwise backward selection using AIC is a widely used criterion to assess model goodness of fit and parsimony 23 , 24 . We assessed the subsequent model improvement through a decrease in the AIC criterion after including all variables in the minimal sufficient adjustment sets plus additional variables not included in our DAG. All variables removed were individually reinserted into the model and reassessed for any model improvement.
53: 
54: #### Predictive performance and model validation
55: 
56: The ability of the variables to predict RSV-positivity in the source population was determined by a tenfold cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve. We constructed Receiver Operator Characteristic (ROC) by plotting the true positive rate (sensitivity) against false positive rate (1-specificity) at various levels of the marker. In k-fold cross validation, the dataset is randomly divided into k approximately equally sized subsamples (or folds) 25 . At each iteration, one-fold is retained as the validation data for testing the model and estimating the Area Under Curve (AUC), while the remaining k − 1 folds are used as training data for model estimation. This process is repeated k times, with each of the k folds used once as the validation data. The ‘ cvauroc’ command in Stata was employed to derive and average the AUCs corresponding to each fold (here k = 10) and bootstrapping the cross-validated AUC was used to obtain statistical inference and bias corrected 95% confidence intervals (CIs). K-fold cross validation avoids the optimistic estimates of predictive performance known to exist when the full dataset is used for assessing model specification and prediction 25 . To explore diagnostic accuracy of the models, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive values (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV) were generated. We determined these characteristics at different false positive rates [eTable 3 ]. However, we chose a 0.5 probability threshold as the cut-off, which maximises sensitivity and specificity of the model. Furthermore, we used a ‘calibration belt’ to evaluate the calibration of our predictive model. The ‘calibration belt’ is a plot depicting the relationship between the model’s fit probabilities and the observed proportions of the response across all ranges of risk, which reflects the reliability or degree of bias of the model 26 . In addition, reliability was tested by the Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test 27 .... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
57: 
58: All data were analysed using STATA v.16.0 28 . We used DAGitty v2.3 to produce the DAG 29 . We conducted a complete case analysis excluding records from the analysis with missing values for one or more of the predictor variables. We calculated incidence rates of predicted RSV-positivity using survival analysis techniques, allowing for multiple hospital admissions per person. We used person-time-at-risk as the denominator (calculated from date of birth until first date of hospital admission). All children were censored at the end of the study period or date of death, whichever was the earlier. Incidence rates were reported per 1000 child-years with associated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) by age group, year of hospital admission, admission season and birth month. Finally, we plotted predicted RSV rates by calendar week throughout the study period.
59: 
60: #### Estimating burden of RSV
61: 
62: After running each logistic regression model, we estimated a predicted probability of RSV-positivity and applied that to all hospital admissions in children aged less than 5 years during the study period given all non-missing variables in the model. All admissions in children aged less than 5 years during the study period with a predicted probability threshold of 0.5 were classified as an RSV-associated admission (hereafter referred to as predicted RSV). Finally, we estimated the under-ascertainment fraction of RSV rates, computed as rate differences between laboratory-confirmed RSV and predicted RSV.
63: 
64: #### Transparency of reporting
65: 
66: The Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD) statement was followed for this study (eTable 4 ) 30 . The TRIPOD statement provides a framework for the full and clear reporting of a prediction model study, such that risk of bias and potential usefulness can be adequately assessed.
67: 
68: #### Ethics statement
69: 
70: The authors assert that all methods were carried out in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations. Ethical approvals were obtained from the WA Department of Health Human Research Ethics Committee and the WA Aboriginal Health Ethics Committee. As the study utilised de-identified linked administrative data, a waiver of informed consent was granted by the WA Department of Health Human Research Ethics Committee.
71: 
72: ## Results
73: 
74: ### Cohort description
75: 
76: From the birth cohort of 321,825 hospitalised children under the age of 5 years at the time of hospital admission, 37,784 were tested for RSV (11.7%). Of these 8,471 (22.4%) were infants aged < 3 months and 5,768 (15.3%) were Aboriginal. From all hospitalised children tested for RSV, laboratory confirmation was determined in 22.8% (n = 8,604 episodes). RSV positivity was more common in children that were younger, non-Aboriginal, male, had mothers with average SES, lived in a metropolitan residence and had hospital admission in the Australian winter months between June and August. One in three (2,594 admissions) of RSV positive admissions were among infants aged < 3 months. Approximately three quarters of all laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive children had a discharge diagnosis of bronchiolitis (Table 1 ).
77: 
78: **Table 1.** Characteristics of laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive admissions used to generate the RSV prediction model, 2000–2012.
79: 
80: ### Predicting RSV positivity
81: 
82: The variables included in the final logistic regression prediction model were child age, gender, delivery route, admission season, Aboriginal status, maternal age, smoking, SES, numbers of siblings, prematurity, admission year, birth year, length of hospital stay, admission to ICU, mechanical ventilation use during admission, maternal history of asthma, any diagnosis code for ALRI and diagnosis code for other infections including unspecified viral illness. To account for seasonality and climatic conditions, we also included season of birth and geographical region of residence respectively (eTable 1 ). The predictive equation of the final model is presented in (eFig. 2 ).
83: 
84: In the multivariable analysis, there was a higher odd of RSV-positivity in those aged < 3 months (Adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = 1.91, 95% CI (1.27–2.87)), and children who were not Aboriginal (AOR = 1.44. 95% CI (1.29–1.61)). RSV-positivity was also significantly associated with a diagnosis of any pneumonia, unspecified ALRI and bronchitis. Similarly, children born in remote or rural areas, who had a long hospital stay (three or more days) and who required mechanical ventilation during admission had an increased odds of RSV positivity.

86: Conversely, prematurity, low SES and maternal history of asthma were associated with reduced odds of RSV-positivity (eTable 2 ).
87:

The sensitivity and specificity of the final model were 58.4% (95% CI 57.3–59.6%), and 92.2% (95% CI 91.8–92.5%) respectively. # Open-Domain Research Answer

You are the EviMed open-domain research assistant: an evidence-based-medicine specialist who writes for expert readers (clinicians, pharmacists, researchers). You give your best professional judgment and label how certain it is. You do not produce academic report packages in conversation — that is the job of the specialist report agents, which the platform routes to when the user explicitly asks for a report.

## Answer first

Structure every substantive answer in this order:

1. **Conclusion / direct answer** — the bottom line in one to three sentences. If the question has an actionable implication (dosing caution, monitoring, interaction, red flag), state it here.
2. **Key evidence** — the few findings that carry the conclusion, with numbered citations. Weigh the evidence; say which way it leans and how strongly.
3. **Uncertainty and evidence level** — what the answer rests on (full text / abstract / bibliographic metadata / established knowledge), what is unknown, and what would change the answer.

Never open with methodology, search narration, or a restatement of the question. Never bury the conclusion at the end.

## Adaptive depth

Match the depth to the question — do not escalate simple questions, and do not superficially answer complex ones:

- **Direct tier** (facts, mechanisms, terminology, definitions, standard dosing): answer from established knowledge in a few sentences to a few paragraphs. No tool calls are required for questions you can answer reliably. Example: 「二甲双胍的作用机制是什么？」 gets a crisp mechanistic answer, not a literature search.
- **Synthesis tier** (comparative effectiveness, safety concerns, "what does the evidence say about X", anything where currency or specific studies matter): run the iterative retrieval loop below, then synthesize across sources into a weighed conclusion. A few short sections are fine; a chat-length answer is the goal.
- **Report tier** (the user explicitly asks for a report, systematic review, 系统评价, 证据报告, or a deliverable document): say briefly that a full evidence report is a separate deliverable, confirm the question, and answer the substance concisely in chat anyway. The platform's deterministic router dispatches explicit report requests to the report pipeline — never try to reproduce that heavy package in conversation.

## Iterative retrieval (synthesis tier)

Retrieve, read, refine — do not stop at one query:

1. Translate the question into 1–3 focused queries (normalize drug names with `drug_term_normalize` when the term is colloquial, brand, or cross-language).
2. Search with `biomedical_source_search` (and `literature_search` / `guideline_search` when configured). Prefer sources that returned abstracts over metadata-only records.
3. Read what you retrieved. When a key source's abstract is insufficient and it is open access, pull the full text with `open_access_full_text` and read the relevant sections.
4. Refine: if results miss the point, rewrite the query (synonyms, population, outcome, study design) and search again. Stop when two consecutive refined queries add no new relevant source, or after three iterations.
5. Deduplicate with `evidence_deduplicate` before synthesizing when the result set is large.

## Evidence honesty (non-negotiable)

- Never fabricate studies, authors, journals, years, DOIs, PMIDs, effect sizes, or URLs. Every numbered citation must correspond to a source you actually retrieved in this turn or to established textbook knowledge stated without a fake citation.
- When retrieval only reached bibliographic metadata (titles, journals, years) for a claim, say so plainly: 「目前仅能检索到题录级证据」and give your best judgment labeled as uncertain. Never present a metadata-only record as if you read its abstract or full text.
- When tools fail, are unconfigured, or return zero results, state the gap and answer from established knowledge with lowered confidence. Never turn an empty search into negative evidence.
- Distinguish established knowledge from retrieved evidence; mark emerging or contested findings as such.
- When an analysis drops records, every count you report must say which set it describes. A table headed with the
  analysed sample size but filled with the full cohort's events gives the reader a rate over the wrong denominator.
  State both — records loaded, records analysed, and the reason for the difference — and take each event count,
  person-time total, and rate from the set the model actually used.
- The reason an input went missing has to be verified, never inferred. When you submit N items and get back fewer,
  check each missing one directly before you explain its absence. Do not reason from the absence to a cause: a
  well-argued subject-matter explanation for a dropped record is the most convincing way to publish a retrieval bug,
  because it reads as a finding and nothing contradicts it. If you cannot confirm why an item is missing, report it
  as unexplained and carry it as a limitation.

## Citation style (reader-friendly)

- Cite as bracketed numbers in prose: `…可降低心血管事件风险 [1]。`
- Collect full source details once, at the end, under `参考文献` / `References`, one numbered entry per source with its HTTPS URL.
- Do not paste raw URLs into prose sentences, do not use inline `[1](https://…)` link syntax, and never emit internal markers such as `<!-- claim:… -->` or `[claim:…]`.
- Only cite sources a reader can open: journal/publisher pages, PubMed/PMC records, guideline or regulator pages, label PDFs. Prefer the HTTPS address, but cite the source's canonical URL as the publisher gives it — some persistent identifiers (for example `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/…`) are canonically http, and rewriting one makes the citation less correct, not more. A fragment is fine when it points at the passage you mean. **Never** cite internal EviMed API routes (`www.evimed.com/api-evimed/…`), gateway URLs, loopback or private addresses, or any URL containing credentials — if a retrieval tool returns such a URL, cite the underlying public source it points to instead. A direct-tier answer with no retrieval needs no citations — do not pad it with honorary references.

## Safety boundary

- Red-flag presentations (chest pain with radiation/diaphoresis, stroke signs, anaphylaxis, suicidal ideation, etc.): lead with the instruction to seek emergency care immediately, then explain.
- High-risk medicines and scenarios (e.g. 速效救心丸 and other pharmacist-flagged medicines, narrow-therapeutic-index drugs, pregnancy, pediatrics, renal/hepatic impairment): state the key safety caveat in the conclusion and recommend confirming with the treating clinician or pharmacist.
- You inform clinical judgment; you do not replace individualized diagnosis or prescribing. Say this once, briefly, only when the question is about a specific patient's management.

## Style

- Use the user's language (Chinese in, Chinese out). Professional, direct, compact.
- Short paragraphs and minimal headings; bullet points only where they genuinely help scanning.
- No boilerplate: no "as an AI" disclaimers, no methodology section, no search-log narration, no padding to look thorough.

## 摘要

呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）是儿童期发病的主要病因之一，但由于对因呼吸道症状住院的患儿缺乏系统性病原检测，基于实验室数据的 RSV 发病率很可能低估了真实疾病负担。本研究采用概率联结的围产期、住院与实验室记录，覆盖 2000–2012 年西澳大利亚（WA）出生的 321 825 名儿童，针对 5 岁以下住院儿童建立 RSV 阳性预测模型，并将该模型应用于全人群队列的全部住院记录，以估计真实 RSV 发病率及低估比例。模型性能以交叉验证的受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC）评价。在 321 825 条住院记录中，37 784 条做了 RSV 检测，其中 22.8% 为阳性。RSV 阳性的预测因素包括更小的入院年龄、男性、非原住民身份、毛细支气管炎诊断以及更长的住院时间。模型显示良好的预测准确性（AUROC 0.87）；灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值与阴性预测值分别为 58.4%、92.2%、68.6% 与 88.3%。对 3 月龄以下儿童，预测的 RSV 住院发病率为 43.7/1000 人年（95% CI 42.1–45.4），而实验室确诊 RSV 住院为 31.7/1000 人年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。研究结果提示，RSV 的真实负担可能比现有估计高 30%–57%。

## 引言

RSV 是全球幼儿发病与死亡的重要原因，每年约有 320 万例被检出的住院事件，且约半数 RSV 相关死亡据估计发生在院外。在澳大利亚，每 10 万名 5 岁以下住院儿童中估计有 418 例为 RSV 所致。本研究团队此前基于人群的研究报告，在 17 岁以下儿童中 RSV 的病原特异发病率为 247/10 万人年，其中出生后前 3 个月的婴儿负担最高（28.1/1000 人年）。RSV 最常与急性毛细支气管炎住院相关，但也见于肺炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染、哮喘、上呼吸道感染以及非特异性病毒诊断编码等其它临床诊断。

在本辖区及别处的人群层面，RSV 检测缺乏系统性安排，且当前不属于法定报告疾病，因此仅凭微生物检测数据集难以估计疾病负担。本团队既往研究显示，17 岁以下儿童中仅约 10% 曾接受 RSV 检测，且检测率随年龄组与年份而变化；此外，54% 因呼吸道感染住院的儿童没有对应的微生物检测记录。随着抗病毒药物、母体疫苗与单克隆抗体的晚期临床试验推进，需要更准确的 RSV 负担估计以支持未来的治疗与预防政策。理解不同人群中 RSV 检测阳性的临床与人口学预测因素，有助于量化基于单一数据集的低估负担；理想情况下需结合临床与实验室数据，英国已针对 1 岁以下婴儿开展过类似研究。

本研究的目的是：建立预测模型，估计西澳大利亚 5 岁以下儿童中 RSV 相关住院的真实发病率，并据此确定仅用实验室记录所得 RSV 发病率的低估比例。

## 方法

### 研究环境与数据来源

西澳大利亚覆盖澳大利亚西部约三分之一区域，2019 年 12 月 31 日人口约 260 万，其中约四分之三居住于温带气候的大珀斯都会区。本研究为基于人群的队列研究，使用西澳大利亚 1996–2012 年全部出生人口的行政联结数据。数据来源包括：围产期信息覆盖率超过 99% 的分娩通知系统、出生与死亡登记、医院患病率数据收集系统以及 PathWest 实验室医学数据库；数据经西澳数据联结局按最佳实践协议进行概率联结。

### 住院数据

纳入入院与出院日期在 2000 年 1 月 1 日至 2012 年 12 月 31 日之间、年龄小于 5 岁的全部住院记录，诊断采用 ICD-10-AM 编码；与既往分析一致，医院间转诊记录被合并。

### 实验室数据

提取 2000 年 1 月 1 日至 2012 年 12 月 31 日间呼吸道标本的 RSV 检测记录，并将标本采集时间在入院日期前后 48 小时内的记录与出生队列个体的住院记录联结；当同一儿童在 48 小时内因不同原因多次住院时，与标本采集日期最近的一次住院联结。研究早期 RSV 主要经免疫荧光抗原检测（占 65%）、病毒培养与补体结合试验检出，后期逐步改用 PCR。据此界定源人群为队列中出生后 5 年内因任何原因住院且具有 RSV 检测记录的儿童（n = 37 784 条住院）。剔除一项或多项变量缺失的 3 801 条记录后，最终纳入预测模型的有 33 983 条含 RSV 检测记录的住院；同样，在剔除缺失值后，对 321 825 条 5 岁以下住院儿童记录估计 RSV 负担。

### 统计分析与模型构建

以 RSV 阳性为二分类结局，对 2000–2012 年期间住院并接受 RSV 检测的 5 岁以下儿童拟合多变量 logistic 回归，使用稳健标准误以校正同一儿童多次住院所致的相关观测。基于文献综述、本机构既往工作及临床合理性共选择 27 个候选预测因素，并采用有向无环图（DAG）指导变量选择。DAG 确定的最小变量集包括儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式、入院季节、原住民身份、母龄、孕期吸烟、社会经济地位、同胞数、胎龄、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长、是否入住重症监护病房（ICU）、是否机械通气、母体哮喘史，以及急性毛细支气管炎、肺炎、支气管炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染、哮喘、上呼吸道感染、百日咳、流感和其它感染（含未特指病毒性疾病、惊厥、发热咳嗽、呼吸异常）的诊断编码；并纳入出生季节与居住地理区域以考虑季节性与气候条件，同时按 Stolwijk 与 Edwards 建议加入正弦与余弦函数刻画 RSV 季节波动。社会经济地位采用澳大利亚统计局在普查区层面的相对优势与劣势指数（SEIFA）。

模型构建采用基于赤池信息准则（AIC）的逐步后向选择；被剔除变量逐一重新纳入并评估是否改善模型。最终模型纳入的变量包括：儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式、入院季节、原住民身份、母龄、吸烟、社会经济地位、同胞数、早产、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长、入住 ICU、机械通气、母体哮喘史、未特指急性下呼吸道感染诊断编码、其它感染诊断编码，以及出生季节、地理区域和季节函数项。

### 性能评价与验证

以十折交叉验证的 AUROC 评价模型预测性能（Stata 的 `cvauroc` 命令，k = 10，并对交叉验证 AUC 做 bootstrap 以获得偏倚校正的 95% 置信区间）；在 0.5 概率阈值下计算灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值（PPV）与阴性预测值（NPV），并用校准带（calibration belt）与 Hosmer–Lemeshow 拟合优度检验评价校准。全部数据分析使用 STATA v16.0，DAG 用 DAGitty v2.3 绘制；采用完全病例分析。发病率采用生存分析技术（以人时风险为分母，自出生日起至首次入院日），按年龄组、入院年份、入院季节与出生月份报告每 1000 人年及 95% CI，并按日历周绘制预测 RSV 率。将 logistic 模型估计的 RSV 阳性概率应用于研究期内全部 5 岁以下住院记录，以 0.5 阈值划分为 RSV 相关住院（即"预测 RSV"），并以实验室确诊与预测 RSV 的率差计算低估比例。报告遵循 TRIPOD 声明。伦理批准来自西澳卫生部人类研究伦理委员会与西澳原住民健康伦理委员会；因使用去标识化的联结行政数据，西澳卫生部人类研究伦理委员会批准免除知情同意。

## 结果

### 队列描述

在 321 825 名 5 岁以下住院儿童中，37 784 例接受 RSV 检测（11.7%），其中 8 471 例（22.4%）为 3 月龄以下婴儿，5 768 例（15.3%）为原住民。检测者中实验室确诊 RSV 阳性占 22.8%（8 604 例次）。RSV 阳性在年龄更小、非原住民、男性、母亲社会经济地位居平均水平、居住于都会区及 6–8 月冬季入院的儿童中更常见；约三分之一（2 594 例次）的 RSV 阳性入院发生在 3 月龄以下婴儿，约四分之三的实验室确诊 RSV 阳性儿童出院诊断为毛细支气管炎。

### RSV 阳性预测

多变量分析中，3 月龄以下（校正比值比 AOR = 1.91，95% CI 1.27–2.87）与非原住民（AOR = 1.44，95% CI 1.29–1.61）儿童的 RSV 阳性几率更高；具有急性毛细支气管炎主诊断或次诊断的儿童 RSV 阳性几率升高约 16 倍（AOR = 16.8，95% CI 15.3–18.5）。肺炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染与支气管炎诊断也与 RSV 阳性显著相关；出生于偏远或农村地区、住院时间较长（≥3 天）及住院期间需机械通气者 RSV 阳性几率升高。反之，早产、低社会经济地位与母体哮喘史与较低的 RSV 阳性几率相关。

十折交叉验证显示模型预测性能稳健（AUROC = 0.87，95% CI 0.86–0.88）；最终模型灵敏度 58.4%（95% CI 57.3–59.6%）、特异度 92.2%（95% CI 91.8–92.5%）、PPV 68.6%（95% CI 67.5–69.7%）、NPV 88.3%（95% CI 87.9–88.7%）。校准带显示模型校准良好，Hosmer–Lemeshow 检验无显著性（P = 0.66）。敏感性分析提示模型性能随实验室检测方法（免疫荧光 vs PCR）略有差异。

### 实验室确诊与预测 RSV 发病率（按入院年龄）

预测 RSV 发病率在更小年龄组更高，以 3 月龄以下婴儿最高：模型预测 3 月龄以下儿童的 RSV 相关住院为 43.7/1000 人年（95% CI 42.1–45.4），而实验室确诊 RSV 住院为 31.7/1000 人年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。预测 RSV 住院率从 12–24 月龄的 5/1000 人年至 3–6 月龄的 28/1000 人年不等。估计的平均年度 RSV 相关住院率，3 月龄以下为 404/1000 名儿童，3–6 月龄为 499/1000 名儿童，6–11 月龄为 302/1000 名儿童，分别对应总住院的低估比例 32%、57% 与 35%。约 76% 的预测 RSV 相关住院发生在 12 月龄以下婴儿，占估计低估量的 39%。12 月龄以下婴儿的预测 RSV 相关住院在冬季达到高峰（n = 6859，204/1000 人年 [95% CI 199.1–208.7]），且以 4–6 月出生者为主；12–24 月龄儿童同样在冬季及 3–5 月出生者中达到高峰。

### 按日历周的 RSV 率

2 岁以下儿童的预测 RSV 住院呈季节性模式，2000–2012 年间每年峰值多出现在第 26–29 周，唯 2007 年峰值出现在第 34 周（66/1000 人年）、2009 年出现在第 32 周（55.9/1000 人年）；实验室确诊 RSV 住院的峰值模式与此一致。

## 讨论

RSV 疫苗研发日益受到全球重视，世界卫生组织已将全球 RSV 疾病负担估计列为优先事项。本研究旨在改进 RSV 发病率估计，以支持疫苗规划倡导并为疫苗影响评价提供基线数据。研究建立了基于人群、基于易获取患者特征的 RSV 相关住院预测模型，性能稳健，可用于识别住院儿童中可能 RSV 阳性者。

基于人群的住院与实验室数据，结果印证了既往关于儿童 RSV 相关住院负担巨大的发现，并提示这一负担被低估超过 30%；负担具有年龄特异性并存在显著季节波动。研究期内，估计的平均年度 RSV 相关住院率在 3 月龄以下为 404/1000 名儿童、2 岁以下为 338/1000 名儿童。RSV 相关住院高峰出现在冬季，且集中于 4、5、6 月出生的婴儿。鉴于低龄婴儿负担最高，未来疫苗规划可将其列为优先受益人群，并已有关于在 RSV 流行季开始时出生的婴儿实施季节性免疫策略的建议。

除年龄更小外，研究还识别出住院时长、毛细支气管炎、肺炎、支气管炎及未特指急性下呼吸道感染等重要预测因素；其中急性毛细支气管炎是最强预测因素，其次为支气管炎，再次为肺炎。英国一项针对婴儿的研究同样报告毛细支气管炎、未特指下呼吸道感染或含 RSV 特异编码者 RSV 阳性几率更高。非原住民及出生于农村或偏远地区者的住院风险更高，偏远与农村地区 RSV 率也最高，可能与家庭拥挤等社会经济劣势及就医可及性有关。值得注意的是，低社会经济地位、早产与哮喘家族史反而与较低的 RSV 阳性几率相关，既往研究亦有类似报告。

十折交叉验证显示模型性能优异且校准良好（AUROC 0.87）；与英国一项预测婴儿 RSV 相关住院（AUROC 0.9）的研究相比，本模型特异度与 NPV 更高，但灵敏度与 PPV 较低。本研究以超过十年的人群住院数据联结实验室与社会人口学记录为基础，纳入既往同类 RSV 预测研究未包含的母体、婴儿与围产期预测因素，并采用 DAG 优化预测因素选择、以 k 折交叉验证校正过度乐观，是主要优势。模型良好拟合了 RSV 相关住院的季节性与年龄分布，但对较大年龄儿童略有低估，可能与围产期之后的风险或生活方式因素数据有限有关。

本研究存在若干局限。第一，结果基于标本采集在入院 48 小时内联结的住院数据，模型仅针对与住院相关的较重 RSV 病例，不估计更广泛的社区 RSV 发病率。第二，仅纳入 2000–2012 年联结数据，未反映更近期的住院趋势，但作者认为模型可应用于更当代的数据，且主要围产期与环境预测因素随时间变化的可能性不大。第三，未纳入母乳喂养、免疫缺陷、托儿所入托及环境因素等潜在预测因素，因这些因素未纳入可用于联结的数据库，但作者预计不会造成重大低估。此外，敏感性分析提示模型性能随实验室检测方法略有差异。

利用人群层面常规实验室与住院数据的联结，本研究建立了预测性能优异、可识别西澳 RSV 相关住院的预测模型，并将其应用于全部 5 岁以下住院儿童，从而估计该州住院儿童的真实 RSV 负担。未来研究需纳入急诊与社区的 RSV 相关就诊、优选加入近期数据及其它潜在预测因素；开发简化风险评分并在其它人群中进行外部验证，亦是模型未来临床应用的考虑方向。

## 结论

本研究成功建立基于人群数据的预测模型，用于估计西澳大利亚住院儿童的真实 RSV 负担，预测性能与内部验证良好。研究结果提示，幼儿中 RSV 的真实负担比仅基于实验室检测数据的估计高 30%–57%。这些估计可作为动态传播模型的输入参数，以更好预测包括母体免疫在内的预防措施的影响。

## 摘要

呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）是儿童期发病的主要病因之一，但由于对因呼吸道症状住院的患儿缺乏系统性病原检测，基于实验室数据的 RSV 发病率很可能低估了真实疾病负担。本研究采用概率联结的围产期、住院与实验室记录，覆盖 2000–2012 年西澳大利亚（WA）出生的 321 825 名儿童，针对 5 岁以下住院儿童建立 RSV 阳性预测模型，并将该模型应用于全人群队列的全部住院记录，以估计真实 RSV 发病率及低估比例。模型性能以交叉验证的受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC）评价。在 321 825 条住院记录中，37 784 条做了 RSV 检测，其中 22.8% 为阳性。RSV 阳性的预测因素包括更小的入院年龄、男性、非原住民身份、毛细支气管炎诊断以及更长的住院时间。模型显示良好的预测准确性（AUROC 0.87）；灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值与阴性预测值分别为 58.4%、92.2%、68.6% 与 88.3%。对 3 月龄以下儿童，预测的 RSV 住院发病率为 43.7/1000 人年（95% CI 42.1–45.4），而实验室确诊 RSV 住院为 31.7/1000 人年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。研究结果提示，RSV 的真实负担可能比现有估计高 30%–57%。

## 引言

RSV 是全球幼儿发病与死亡的重要原因，每年约有 320 万例被检出的住院事件，且约半数 RSV 相关死亡据估计发生在院外。在澳大利亚，每 10 万名 5 岁以下住院儿童中估计有 418 例为 RSV 所致。本研究团队此前基于人群的研究报告，在 17 岁以下儿童中 RSV 的病原特异发病率为 247/10 万人年，其中出生后前 3 个月的婴儿负担最高（28.1/1000 人年）。RSV 最常与急性毛细支气管炎住院相关，但也见于肺炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染、哮喘、上呼吸道感染以及非特异性病毒诊断编码等其它临床诊断。

在本辖区及别处的人群层面，RSV 检测缺乏系统性安排，且当前不属于法定报告疾病，因此仅凭微生物检测数据集难以估计疾病负担。本团队既往研究显示，17 岁以下儿童中仅约 10% 曾接受 RSV 检测，且检测率随年龄组与年份而变化；此外，54% 因呼吸道感染住院的儿童没有对应的微生物检测记录。随着抗病毒药物、母体疫苗与单克隆抗体的晚期临床试验推进，需要更准确的 RSV 负担估计以支持未来的治疗与预防政策。理解不同人群中 RSV 检测阳性的临床与人口学预测因素，有助于量化基于单一数据集的低估负担；理想情况下需结合临床与实验室数据，英国已针对 1 岁以下婴儿开展过类似研究。

本研究的目的是：建立预测模型，估计西澳大利亚 5 岁以下儿童中 RSV 相关住院的真实发病率，并据此确定仅用实验室记录所得 RSV 发病率的低估比例。

## 方法

### 研究环境与数据来源

西澳大利亚覆盖澳大利亚西部约三分之一区域，2019 年 12 月 31 日人口约 260 万，其中约四分之三居住于温带气候的大珀斯都会区。本研究为基于人群的队列研究，使用西澳大利亚 1996–2012 年全部出生人口的行政联结数据。数据来源包括：围产期信息覆盖率超过 99% 的分娩通知系统、出生与死亡登记、医院患病率数据收集系统以及 PathWest 实验室医学数据库；数据经西澳数据联结局按最佳实践协议进行概率联结。

### 住院数据

纳入入院与出院日期在 2000 年 1 月 1 日至 2012 年 12 月 31 日之间、年龄小于 5 岁的全部住院记录，诊断采用 ICD-10-AM 编码；与既往分析一致，医院间转诊记录被合并。

### 实验室数据

提取 2000 年 1 月 1 日至 2012 年 12 月 31 日间呼吸道标本的 RSV 检测记录，并将标本采集时间在入院日期前后 48 小时内的记录与出生队列个体的住院记录联结；当同一儿童在 48 小时内因不同原因多次住院时，与标本采集日期最近的一次住院联结。研究早期 RSV 主要经免疫荧光抗原检测（占 65%）、病毒培养与补体结合试验检出，后期逐步改用 PCR。据此界定源人群为队列中出生后 5 年内因任何原因住院且具有 RSV 检测记录的儿童（n = 37 784 条住院）。剔除一项或多项变量缺失的 3 801 条记录后，最终纳入预测模型的有 33 983 条含 RSV 检测记录的住院；同样，在剔除缺失值后，对 321 825 条 5 岁以下住院儿童记录估计 RSV 负担。

### 统计分析与模型构建

以 RSV 阳性为二分类结局，对 2000–2012 年期间住院并接受 RSV 检测的 5 岁以下儿童拟合多变量 logistic 回归，使用稳健标准误以校正同一儿童多次住院所致的相关观测。基于文献综述、本机构既往工作及临床合理性共选择 27 个候选预测因素，并采用有向无环图（DAG）指导变量选择。DAG 确定的最小变量集包括儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式、入院季节、原住民身份、母龄、孕期吸烟、社会经济地位、同胞数、胎龄、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长、是否入住重症监护病房（ICU）、是否机械通气、母体哮喘史，以及急性毛细支气管炎、肺炎、支气管炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染、哮喘、上呼吸道感染、百日咳、流感和其它感染（含未特指病毒性疾病、惊厥、发热咳嗽、呼吸异常）的诊断编码；并纳入出生季节与居住地理区域以考虑季节性与气候条件，同时按 Stolwijk 与 Edwards 建议加入正弦与余弦函数刻画 RSV 季节波动。社会经济地位采用澳大利亚统计局在普查区层面的相对优势与劣势指数（SEIFA）。

模型构建采用基于赤池信息准则（AIC）的逐步后向选择；被剔除变量逐一重新纳入并评估是否改善模型。最终模型纳入的变量包括：儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式、入院季节、原住民身份、母龄、吸烟、社会经济地位、同胞数、早产、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长、入住 ICU、机械通气、母体哮喘史、未特指急性下呼吸道感染诊断编码、其它感染诊断编码，以及出生季节、地理区域和季节函数项。

### 性能评价与验证

以十折交叉验证的 AUROC 评价模型预测性能（Stata 的 `cvauroc` 命令，k = 10，并对交叉验证 AUC 做 bootstrap 以获得偏倚校正的 95% 置信区间）；在 0.5 概率阈值下计算灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值（PPV）与阴性预测值（NPV），并用校准带（calibration belt）与 Hosmer–Lemeshow 拟合优度检验评价校准。全部数据分析使用 STATA v16.0，DAG 用 DAGitty v2.3 绘制；采用完全病例分析。发病率采用生存分析技术（以人时风险为分母，自出生日起至首次入院日），按年龄组、入院年份、入院季节与出生月份报告每 1000 人年及 95% CI，并按日历周绘制预测 RSV 率。将 logistic 模型估计的 RSV 阳性概率应用于研究期内全部 5 岁以下住院记录，以 0.5 阈值划分为 RSV 相关住院（即"预测 RSV"），并以实验室确诊与预测 RSV 的率差计算低估比例。报告遵循 TRIPOD 声明。伦理批准来自西澳卫生部人类研究伦理委员会与西澳原住民健康伦理委员会；因使用去标识化的联结行政数据，西澳卫生部人类研究伦理委员会批准免除知情同意。

## 结果

### 队列描述

在 321 825 名 5 岁以下住院儿童中，37 784 例接受 RSV 检测（11.7%），其中 8 471 例（22.4%）为 3 月龄以下婴儿，5 768 例（15.3%）为原住民。检测者中实验室确诊 RSV 阳性占 22.8%（8 604 例次）。RSV 阳性在年龄更小、非原住民、男性、母亲社会经济地位居平均水平、居住于都会区及 6–8 月冬季入院的儿童中更常见；约三分之一（2 594 例次）的 RSV 阳性入院发生在 3 月龄以下婴儿，约四分之三的实验室确诊 RSV 阳性儿童出院诊断为毛细支气管炎。

### RSV 阳性预测

多变量分析中，3 月龄以下（校正比值比 AOR = 1.91，95% CI 1.27–2.87）与非原住民（AOR = 1.44，95% CI 1.29–1.61）儿童的 RSV 阳性几率更高；具有急性毛细支气管炎主诊断或次诊断的儿童 RSV 阳性几率升高约 16 倍（AOR = 16.8，95% CI 15.3–18.5）。肺炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染与支气管炎诊断也与 RSV 阳性显著相关；出生于偏远或农村地区、住院时间较长（≥3 天）及住院期间需机械通气者 RSV 阳性几率升高。反之，早产、低社会经济地位与母体哮喘史与较低的 RSV 阳性几率相关。

十折交叉验证显示模型预测性能稳健（AUROC = 0.87，95% CI 0.86–0.88）；最终模型灵敏度 58.4%（95% CI 57.3–59.6%）、特异度 92.2%（95% CI 91.8–92.5%）、PPV 68.6%（95% CI 67.5–69.7%）、NPV 88.3%（95% CI 87.9–88.7%）。校准带显示模型校准良好，Hosmer–Lemeshow 检验无显著性（P = 0.66）。敏感性分析提示模型性能随实验室检测方法（免疫荧光 vs PCR）略有差异。

### 实验室确诊与预测 RSV 发病率（按入院年龄）

预测 RSV 发病率在更小年龄组更高，以 3 月龄以下婴儿最高：模型预测 3 月龄以下儿童的 RSV 相关住院为 43.7/1000 人年（95% CI 42.1–45.4），而实验室确诊 RSV 住院为 31.7/1000 人年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。预测 RSV 住院率从 12–24 月龄的 5/1000 人年至 3–6 月龄的 28/1000 人年不等。估计的平均年度 RSV 相关住院率，3 月龄以下为 404/1000 名儿童，3–6 月龄为 499/1000 名儿童，6–11 月龄为 302/1000 名儿童，分别对应总住院的低估比例 32%、57% 与 35%。约 76% 的预测 RSV 相关住院发生在 12 月龄以下婴儿，占估计低估量的 39%。12 月龄以下婴儿的预测 RSV 相关住院在冬季达到高峰（n = 6859，204/1000 人年 [95% CI 199.1–208.7]），且以 4–6 月出生者为主；12–24 月龄儿童同样在冬季及 3–5 月出生者中达到高峰。

### 按日历周的 RSV 率

2 岁以下儿童的预测 RSV 住院呈季节性模式，2000–2012 年间每年峰值多出现在第 26–29 周，唯 2007 年峰值出现在第 34 周（66/1000 人年）、2009 年出现在第 32 周（55.9/1000 人年）；实验室确诊 RSV 住院的峰值模式与此一致。

## 讨论

RSV 疫苗研发日益受到全球重视，世界卫生组织已将全球 RSV 疾病负担估计列为优先事项。本研究旨在改进 RSV 发病率估计，以支持疫苗规划倡导并为疫苗影响评价提供基线数据。研究建立了基于人群、基于易获取患者特征的 RSV 相关住院预测模型，性能稳健，可用于识别住院儿童中可能 RSV 阳性者。

基于人群的住院与实验室数据，结果印证了既往关于儿童 RSV 相关住院负担巨大的发现，并提示这一负担被低估超过 30%；负担具有年龄特异性并存在显著季节波动。研究期内，估计的平均年度 RSV 相关住院率在 3 月龄以下为 404/1000 名儿童、2 岁以下为 338/1000 名儿童。RSV 相关住院高峰出现在冬季，且集中于 4、5、6 月出生的婴儿。鉴于低龄婴儿负担最高，未来疫苗规划可将其列为优先受益人群，并已有关于在 RSV 流行季开始时出生的婴儿实施季节性免疫策略的建议。

除年龄更小外，研究还识别出住院时长、毛细支气管炎、肺炎、支气管炎及未特指急性下呼吸道感染等重要预测因素；其中急性毛细支气管炎是最强预测因素，其次为支气管炎，再次为肺炎。英国一项针对婴儿的研究同样报告毛细支气管炎、未特指下呼吸道感染或含 RSV 特异编码者 RSV 阳性几率更高。非原住民及出生于农村或偏远地区者的住院风险更高，偏远与农村地区 RSV 率也最高，可能与家庭拥挤等社会经济劣势及就医可及性有关。值得注意的是，低社会经济地位、早产与哮喘家族史反而与较低的 RSV 阳性几率相关，既往研究亦有类似报告。

十折交叉验证显示模型性能优异且校准良好（AUROC 0.87）；与英国一项预测婴儿 RSV 相关住院（AUROC 0.9）的研究相比，本模型特异度与 NPV 更高，但灵敏度与 PPV 较低。本研究以超过十年的人群住院数据联结实验室与社会人口学记录为基础，纳入既往同类 RSV 预测研究未包含的母体、婴儿与围产期预测因素，并采用 DAG 优化预测因素选择、以 k 折交叉验证校正过度乐观，是主要优势。模型良好拟合了 RSV 相关住院的季节性与年龄分布，但对较大年龄儿童略有低估，可能与围产期之后的风险或生活方式因素数据有限有关。

本研究存在若干局限。第一，结果基于标本采集在入院 48 小时内联结的住院数据，模型仅针对与住院相关的较重 RSV 病例，不估计更广泛的社区 RSV 发病率。第二，仅纳入 2000–2012 年联结数据，未反映更近期的住院趋势，但作者认为模型可应用于更当代的数据，且主要围产期与环境预测因素随时间变化的可能性不大。第三，未纳入母乳喂养、免疫缺陷、托儿所入托及环境因素等潜在预测因素，因这些因素未纳入可用于联结的数据库，但作者预计不会造成重大低估。此外，敏感性分析提示模型性能随实验室检测方法略有差异。

利用人群层面常规实验室与住院数据的联结，本研究建立了预测性能优异、可识别西澳 RSV 相关住院的预测模型，并将其应用于全部 5 岁以下住院儿童，从而估计该州住院儿童的真实 RSV 负担。未来研究需纳入急诊与社区的 RSV 相关就诊、优选加入近期数据及其它潜在预测因素；开发简化风险评分并在其它人群中进行外部验证，亦是模型未来临床应用的考虑方向。

## 结论

本研究成功建立基于人群数据的预测模型，用于估计西澳大利亚住院儿童的真实 RSV 负担，预测性能与内部验证良好。研究结果提示，幼儿中 RSV 的真实负担比仅基于实验室检测数据的估计高 30%–57%。这些估计可作为动态传播模型的输入参数，以更好预测包括母体免疫在内的预防措施的影响。

## 来源忠实性说明（逐项核对）

本重写的事实底稿为开放获取全文 **PMC8748465 / DOI 10.1038/s41598-021-04080-3**，关键数值均已在正文各节中定位（方法中的样本量与分母、结果中的 AUROC/灵敏度/特异度/PPV/NPV、各年龄组发病率与低估比例、讨论中的作者自述局限性、结论中的 30%–57%）。以下几点需特别说明：

1. **勘误（Author Correction，2024）**：原文 Table 1 中"胎龄"变量下「RSV-positive N (%)」一列数值曾互相错位，连带导致「Total admissions N (%)」与「RSV positivity rate (%)」错误，2024 年已发布更正（DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-52791-0）。该勘误仅涉及表 1 的胎龄分布，不影响模型结果、AUROC、发病率及结论。本重写正文未引用被勘误的胎龄分布数值。
2. **单位差异**：原文摘要中预测发病率以「每 1000 人年」表示（如 3 月龄以下 43.7/1000 人年），而结果与讨论中"平均年度住院率"以「每 1000 名儿童」表示（如 3 月龄以下 404/1000 名儿童）。两者在原文中并存，本重写按原文各自单位如实保留，未作换算或"纠正"。
3. **样本量口径**：321 825 为 5 岁以下住院儿童记录数（用于负担估计）；37 784 为接受 RSV 检测的住院数；剔除缺失后进入最终模型为 33 983 条住院；实验室确诊 RSV 阳性为 8 604 例次。各数字对应口径已在正文中分别注明。
4. **未编造内容**：局限性段落仅收录作者在原文明确陈述的条目；未补写仓库地址、引用量、预印本标识或实施状态等原文未明示的内容。引言中的背景发病率数字（如每年 320 万检出住院、418/10 万、247/10 万人年、28.1/1000 人年等）均为原文引言所陈述、并引证其既往文献（Shi et al. 2017 Lancet；Saravanos et al. 2019 MJA；Lim et al. 2017；Moore et al. 2020 J Infect Dis；Reeves et al. 2019 J Infect），本重写仅忠实转述原文框架，不将其当作本次建模直接产出。
